checks.label: all required study-readiness cases are present
dyadic archive-control edge cases are explicit
optional AI branch cites reporting and risk-governance anchors

cases.label: dyadic consent
cases.participant_right: Both partners consent separately; one partner's agreement never stands in for the other.
cases.protocol_requirement: Consent form and intake script record partner-specific consent, archive permission, and contact limits.

cases.label: deletion control
cases.participant_right: Each partner can request deletion of identifiable archive material before analysis lock.
cases.protocol_requirement: Protocol names who can delete, what is deleted, when deletion closes, and how derived data are handled.

cases.label: export control
cases.participant_right: Participants can receive their own drawings and approved shared artifacts in a usable format.
cases.protocol_requirement: Export workflow separates personal copies, shared copies, de-identified research data, and public examples.

cases.label: replay control
cases.participant_right: Participants are told when stroke replay exists and can decline replay use beyond the session.
cases.protocol_requirement: Replay logs require explicit permission, purpose limits, access logs, and redaction before presentation.

cases.label: redaction
cases.participant_right: Participants can flag names, symbols, locations, or sensitive marks for masking before sharing.
cases.protocol_requirement: Redaction procedure preserves audit trails while removing identifying or partner-sensitive content.

cases.label: withdrawal
cases.participant_right: Either partner can withdraw from future participation without penalty or partner permission.
cases.protocol_requirement: Withdrawal script explains what happens to collected, de-identified, exported, and jointly authored data.

cases.label: adverse event
cases.participant_right: Participants know how to pause, stop, or report distress, conflict, or privacy discomfort.
cases.protocol_requirement: Protocol defines adverse-event triage, escalation contacts, stopping rules, and follow-up documentation.

cases.label: data retention
cases.participant_right: Participants are told how long raw marks, replay logs, exports, and analysis tables are retained.
cases.protocol_requirement: Retention schedule distinguishes raw identifiable files, de-identified tables, derived metrics, and figures.

cases.label: one partner disagrees
cases.participant_right: If partners disagree about saving, replay, export, or publication, the stricter privacy choice governs.
cases.protocol_requirement: Dyadic conflict rule defaults to non-retention or de-identification unless both partners approve sharing.

cases.label: intervention description
cases.participant_right: Participants and reviewers can see what the drawing activity asks people to do.
cases.protocol_requirement: TIDieR-style description records materials, procedures, session dose, tailoring, modifications, and fidelity.

cases.label: AI branch governance
cases.participant_right: AI support is optional, disclosed, rejectable, reversible, and never described as a partner.
cases.protocol_requirement: Optional AI studies require a separate arm, risk-management log, CONSORT-AI/SPIRIT-AI fields, and EU AI Act check.

cases.label: PRISMA boundary
cases.participant_right: Participants are not affected because the current manuscript does not make a systematic-review claim.
cases.protocol_requirement: Activate PRISMA only if the evidence synthesis is redesigned as a systematic review.
